amendments.why: Rule 52 named only the complementizer and then said that where the ASV writes no complementizer there is nothing to place and the lamed goes unrepresented. That sentence is narrower than what the corpus does and is what EZK.17.14 got wrong: the ASV recast one of the verse's two lamed-infinitives as a gerund and wrote 'by' for it, and the verse pass read 'no complementizer' as 'nothing to place' for the other lamed while giving the linearly first one the 'that'. Amended in place rather than added as a new rule so the over-broad sentence does not stand for whoever reads it first.
amendments.replaced: Where the ASV writes no complementizer at all there is nothing to place, and the `לְ` goes `unrepresented` under rule 40.
amendments.basis: corpus-query LEMMA=לְ NEXT=Vqc LIKE=EZK.17 over the finished OT chapters: 1271 units in 284 chapters. Aligned to a written 'to' in 583, 'that' in 81, and 'for' (13), 'in' (13), 'of' (13), 'after' (6), 'when' (4), 'by' (3) and smaller groups in 53 more; unrepresented in 527. The two groups do not contradict each other: the unrepresented ones are recastings that write no function word at all (GEN.11.8 'left off building', 1KI.9.1 'the building of the house', HOS.4.10, GEN.4.2, ISA.23.12, ISA.30.5, ISA.44.28), while every gerund with a written preposition takes it (EXO.38.27 'for casting', 1KI.1.41 and ISA.33.1 'an end of eating/of dealing', 1KI.3.1 'an end of building', EZK.14.13 and PSA.78.18 and PSA.119.9 'by ...'). So the amendment records what the corpus already does rather than a new claim.

report: This reconciliation was run by hand in an interactive session. The driver's own reconcile pass failed at zero turns on a session limit ('You've hit your session limit'), and the run's cost ledger records that failure rather than this pass; nothing here was paid for through data/driver/EZK.17/reconcile.json. A standing directive in this session forbids spawning subagents unless the user asks, so the delegation the reconcile briefing calls for was not used and every investigation below was made in the parent, as that section itself directs when a directive forbids it.

Task 1, cross-verse consistency: read all 58 candidate lemma groups and the 593-unit dump end to end. One real split, already corrected before this session ran out of tokens and left in the working tree: EZK.17.14 had given the 'that' of 'that by keeping his covenant it might stand' to the lamed of לִשְׁמֹר and the 'by' to the infinitive שְׁמֹר, leaving the lamed of לְעָמְדָהּ unrepresented. The corrected verse gives 'by' to the gerund's lamed and 'that' to the lamed whose infinitive the finite clause renders, which is what 17.15 ('in sending') and 17.18 ('by breaking') already did and what rule 52's counting sentence directs; its receipt was re-marked and the file validates. Nothing else in the table is a split: the article buckets in 17.3 and 17.7 are places where the ASV writes no 'the' (rule 29) against places where it writes one, the הֲ buckets are rule 17's own three cases (particle with a fronted auxiliary, particle with inversion alone in 17.12, and a fronted auxiliary in 17.7, 17.9 and 17.15 where the source writes no particle at all), and the repeated-preposition and resultative-lamed buckets are rules 22, 40 and 21 applied to different clauses.

The added-versus-folded question the briefing asks up front: all 12 added units were re-tested for a licensing morpheme and none was found. Six are supplied object pronouns in clauses with no object morpheme (17.5, 17.12, 17.21, 17.22 twice, 17.24; rule 44), and every clause where a suffix does stand keeps its pronoun with that suffix (17.4, 17.13, 17.19, 17.23), so the boundary is drawn the same way throughout. The others are the coordinating 'and' between two asyndetic descriptive phrases in 17.3, the second 'that' of 17.9 whose clause is asyndetic, the contrastive 'but' of 17.14, the supplied 'dwelleth' and appositional 'even' of 17.16, and the supplied possessive 'his' of 17.17 where חַיִל carries no suffix. The two competing readings worth naming - 17.9's 'that' as a rewriting of the first waw's 'that' under rule 25, and 17.14's 'but that' as one rendering of a lamed under rule 55 - are named in those units' own notes; both were rejected because rule 55's coordinator-plus-subordinator pair governs a waw and no waw stands in either clause.

Task 2, BSB: none of the 31 disagreements is a genuine error. They are the documented convention difference in four classes - ASV-recast prepositions the ASV spends no word on (11 across 8 verses), the suffix of אֲדֹנָי (5, rule 22), articles for which the ASV writes no 'the' (9 in 17.3 and 17.7, rule 29), and object markers with a bare English object (4, rule 16). The three singletons are the same kinds: the resumptive suffix of אֲשֶׁר לוֹ in 17.3, which rule 22 leaves unrendered because the relative is the subject; the interrogative הֲ of 17.12, where the ASV marks the question by inversion alone, which is rule 17's own case; and the first waw of 17.15, where the ASV's single 'and yet' stands before the last clause and rule 42's count gives it to the second waw. No accepted edge was changed to improve the rate.

Task 3, promotion: rule 52 amended in place and the contract bumped from ot-hebrew-verse-v88 to ot-hebrew-verse-v89. The version was v87 when this chapter was aligned and had already moved to v88 under another chapter's reconciliation while this one worked, so the edit was built from the file as it read then, with its version and highest rule number parsed and asserted before writing. No rule was renumbered and no new number was added.

No conventions recorded. The 56 repeated note texts the report counts are verse passes restating rules the contract already binds every verse with - the divine name, the waw of rule 14, suffixes under rule 18, construct chains under rules 19 and 29, the interrogative under rule 17 - and the one judgment that was not already in the contract is now rule 52 rather than a chapter log entry. Recording restatements would only hide a real convention if a later chapter needs one.

Every finishing check passed on the recompiled chapter: 593 units over all 588 selected Hebrew tokens and all 770 ASV tokens in 24 verses, 12 added, 535 aligned, 46 unrepresented, 24 of 24 receipts current and all naming ot-hebrew-verse-v87, the version the chapter was aligned under.
